statement: Given a set of vectors $v_1, \dots, v_n$ in an inner product space, the Gram matrix (or Gramian matrix) $G$ is the $n \times n$ matrix whose entries are given by the inner products $G_{ij} = \langle v_i, v_j \rangle$. When the vectors are the columns of a matrix $X$, the Gram matrix is $G = X^{\dagger}X$ in the general complex case, which simplifies to $G = X^{\top}X$ when vector coordinates are real numbers.

symbols.dimensions: m x 1 (or element of inner product space)

symbols.meaning: matrix whose columns are the vectors v_1, ..., v_n
(i, j)-th entry of the Gram matrix

properties.property: The Gram matrix is Hermitian in the complex case (G = G^†) and symmetric in the real case (G = G^⊤).
properties.why: Follows directly from the conjugate symmetry of the inner product, G_ji = ⟨v_j, v_i⟩ = ⟨v_i, v_j⟩* = G_ij*

properties.property: The Gram matrix is positive semidefinite, and is positive definite if and only if the vectors v_1, ..., v_n are linearly independent.
properties.why: For any coordinate vector x, x^† G x = ‖∑_i x_i v_i‖^2 ≥ 0, which is strictly positive for x ≠ 0 iff the vectors are linearly independent

properties.property: A set of vectors is linearly independent if and only if the Gram determinant det(G) is non-zero.
properties.why: The Gram determinant corresponds to the square of the n-dimensional volume of the parallelotope spanned by the vectors, which vanishes iff they are dependent

properties.property: The rank of the Gram matrix equals the dimension of the subspace spanned by the vectors.
properties.why: Linear dependencies among the vectors correspond to the null space of G

assumptions.assumption: The vectors v_1, ..., v_n belong to a vector space equipped with an inner product (or bilinear form).
assumptions.breaks_when: No inner product or bilinear pairing is defined on the underlying vector space.

assumptions.assumption: For function spaces, the functions are square-integrable on the interval [t_0, t_f].
assumptions.breaks_when: The functions are not square-integrable, causing the inner product integral to diverge.

failure_modes.cause: The vectors v_1, ..., v_n are linearly dependent (such as when n > m for vectors in R^m or C^m).
